audit.workflowIntro: Read-only log of admin mutations to Professional Worlds (verticals, modules, packs, rollouts, etc.). Filters query the server; the list paginates locally in pages of {{pageSize}}.
audit.workflowStep1: Leave filters empty and click Apply to load the latest slice (capped by the server limit). Narrow by entity type, risk label, or admin user UUID when investigating an incident.
audit.workflowStep2: Click a row in the middle panel to load before/after details on the right.
audit.workflowStep3: Structured details are admin-only copies for forensics — do not treat them as live configuration for the desktop runtime.
audit.workflowStep4: Use Reset filters to clear inputs and reload the unfiltered list.
audit.filtersIntro: All fields are optional; values are passed as query parameters to the audit API.
audit.helpEntityType: Filter by `entity_type` string from the backend (examples: vertical, module, pack_release, rollout).
audit.helpRiskLevel: Exact match on stored risk label if present (e.g. normal, high). Leave empty to ignore.
audit.helpActorId: UUID of the admin user attributed in the row. Empty includes rows attributed to the system.
audit.fetchLimitNote: Each request fetches at most {{limit}} rows from the server; pagination below only pages the loaded set.
audit.eventsListLead: Newest-first within the loaded batch. Select a row to inspect details on the right.
audit.emptyEventsTitle: No audit rows in this batch
audit.emptyEventsLead: Try clearing filters and applying again, or narrow criteria if the result set is empty.

audit.afterHelper: Record state after the change. This is operator evidence for verification.

packs.workflowIntro: Prepare pack JSON, review without writes, run an import preview, then confirm. Version + release ship changes to users.
packs.workflowStep1: Pick a pack version on the left (its id is filled on the right) or click Export from production — the live manifest fills the editor and downloads as a file.
packs.workflowStep2: Edit JSON manually or upload a .json file up to 2 MB. Invalid JSON shows an error on the next action.
packs.workflowStep3: Compare to production is read-only: differences and risks only; the database is unchanged.
packs.workflowStep4: Import preview simulates applying the manifest: a report JSON appears below. Verify it looks right.
packs.workflowStep5: Confirm import writes the manifest into pack data; only after a successful preview.
packs.workflowStep6: Save pack version stores the manifest as a new pack version with label and changelog.
packs.workflowStep7: Releases: draft release → approve → publish or rollback — follow your change process.
packs.editorActionsTitle: Actions on the manifest in the editor
packs.helpExport: Copy what users currently have in production.
packs.helpDiff: Compare editor contents to production with no database changes.
packs.helpDryRun: Simulate import and get a report; nothing is applied yet.
packs.helpConfirmImport: Apply the manifest to pack data. Use only after a successful preview.
packs.versionsHint: Click a version row to copy its id into the Release fields on the right.
packs.importJobJsonHelper: Dry-run import report: verify counts and risks before confirm.
packs.diffJsonHelper: Full diff object for operators; risk summary cards appear above.
packs.uploadHint: Only JSON object files up to 2 MB are accepted before the import preview.
packs.manifestRecoveryHint: If an action reports a JSON error, return to the last production export or upload a validated .json file; the editor expects one manifest object, not an array.
packs.uploadTooLarge: Manifest file is too large. Maximum size is {{size}}.
packs.placeholderPackVersionId: Pack version ID when creating from a specific version
packs.approveLead: Review the loaded diff risk summary before approving.
packs.noDiffRisksLoaded: No diff risk summary is loaded for this release.

rollouts.workflowIntro: Rollouts bind a published pack release to how users on this vertical receive the new runtime pack. Create a row on the left, then operate it from the list on the right (pause, resume, retarget).
rollouts.workflowStep1: On the Packs tab: save a pack version, create a release, approve it, publish — you need the published release UUID, not a draft or pack version ID.
rollouts.workflowStep2: Paste the published release ID here, choose a mode (everyone / gradual % / allowlist / off), then Create rollout. The server stores one rollout row per release and configuration.
rollouts.workflowStep3: Estimated audience is only for the preview math in this form; it is not loaded from analytics.
rollouts.workflowStep4: Creating or updating a rollout bumps the vertical runtime epoch so clients can pick up changes.
rollouts.workflowStep5: Pause stops rollout delivery without deleting the row; Edit targeting + Save changes mode and stored percentage.
rollouts.createFormLead: Start a new rollout for this vertical. Use a release that is already published.
rollouts.activePanelLead: Rollouts already created for this vertical. Cards show mode, pause state, and identifiers; use the actions to change behaviour safely.
rollouts.emptyStateTitle: No rollouts for this vertical yet
rollouts.emptyStateLead: After you create one, it appears here with controls.
rollouts.emptyStateHint1: If you have no published release ID: open the Packs tab — import or save a manifest version, create a draft release, approve, then publish.
rollouts.emptyStateHint2: Copy the published release ID into the field on the left, pick a mode, then press Create rollout.
rollouts.emptyStateHint3: You may have several rollout rows over time; check pause state and updated_at when coordinating with other operators.
rollouts.releaseIdPlaceholder: Published release ID from the Packs tab
rollouts.helpReleaseId: UUID of a published release from the Packs tab (not a draft release id before publish).
rollouts.helpMode: How users are selected for this rollout. A short explanation for the current mode appears under the list.
rollouts.helpPercentage: Applies when mode is «Audience percentage». For other modes the value is still stored on the row but the preview meter uses fixed rules.
rollouts.helpAudience: Rough planning number for preview counts in this UI only.
rollouts.previewExplain: Preview is illustrative. Allowlist mode does not estimate a user count in this panel.

modeDescriptions.all: Immediate: eligible users on this vertical receive the published release bundle without a gradual ramp.
modeDescriptions.percentage: Gradual: only the stored percentage of eligible users receives the rollout until you raise it or change mode.
modeDescriptions.allowlist: Only accounts on the server-managed rollout allowlist receive it. This UI does not show or edit the allowlist.
modeDescriptions.disabled: Row exists but rollout does not deliver this release to users — a hard off switch while keeping history.
